definitions.explanation: the physical telephone device or handset, as distinct from the service or act of calling

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{電話機|でんわき}を{買|か}った。
{電話機|でんわき}の{受話器|じゅわき}を{取|と}ってください。
examples.english: Please pick up the telephone receiver.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}の{電話機|でんわき}はダイヤル{式|しき}で、{番号|ばんごう}を{回|まわ}して{掛|か}けるものだった。
examples.english: Old telephones were rotary-dial type, where you dialed by turning the numbers.

notes:
Composed of {電話|でんわ} (telephone) and {機|き} (machine, device). While {電話|でんわ} can refer to both the device and the act of calling, {電話機|でんわき} specifically refers to the physical telephone device itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {電話機|でんわき}を{設置|せっち}する: to install a telephone
- {電話機|でんわき}の{故障|こしょう}: telephone malfunction
- {固定|こてい}{電話機|でんわき}: landline telephone
- {公衆|こうしゅう}{電話機|でんわき}: public telephone

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {電話|でんわ}: telephone — the general word, refers to both the device and phone calls
- {受話器|じゅわき}: receiver, handset — the part you hold to your ear
- {携帯電話|けいたいでんわ}: mobile phone — portable telephone
- {固定電話|こていでんわ}: landline — a non-mobile telephone line
